morgan: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak rolled yesterday we started seeing an ~18% drop in EU (eu-west) prefix cache hit-rate vs baseline. Routing shows more fallbacks to us-west and some tail latency spikes. :thinking:

chen: Can you paste a short example of the routing decision & cache log? wondering if key canonicalization changed with the new tokenization kernel.

morgan: Pasting a trimmed log slice:```
2026-12-03T12:05:14Z region=eu-west route_decision=LOCAL_CACHE check_key="/prompt/checkout/abc123" result=MISS
2026-12-03T12:05:14Z region=eu-west fallback_region=us-west route_cost_ms=420 cache_hit=false replication_age_ms=2100
2026-12-03T12:05:14Z region=eu-west route_decision=LOCAL_CACHE check_key="/prompt/checkout/ABC123" result=HIT
```
This smells like non-deterministic key normalization between the inference path and the cache key generator.

sara: We changed batching heuristics at the same time — kernel now prefers fused attention which slightly alters tokenization offsets for some inputs. If the cache key uses raw prompt string vs normalized tokens that could explain case/whitespace differences. Quick canonicalization we use locally:```
def canonicalize_prefix(s):
    s = s.strip()
    s = s.replace('\n', ' ')
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", ' ', s)
    return s.lower()
```
Can we validate whether cache-layer applies same function?

nate: Also seeing replication_cf_lag spike in eu cluster during the same window: `replication_cf_lag.p95` jumps from ~120ms to ~2s. That exacerbates misses because we route away when local replica reports miss but remote has it. Suggest we add a short heartbeat TTL adjustment and a tombstone window to reduce false misses.

perf-bot: ALERT perf.prefetch-cache-hit-rate.eu drop=18% window=5m severity=warning

deploy-bot: Deployed: kernel-selection=attention-fused v2 -> canary 100% at 2026-12-03T11:58:02Z by @release-bot

chen: Mitigation plan (fast): 1) temporarily bias routing priority to prefer local region for up to 300ms even on miss; 2) enable aggressive key canonicalization in cache lookup layer; 3) disable kernel change on a quick rollback if canary shows sustained degradation. Example route tweak:```
routing.priority = [LOCAL, REMOTE]
routing.local_pref_max_ms = 300
```
We should be careful with throughput impact but it's a quick safety valve.

morgan: Sounds good. I'll open a canary for EU with routing.local_pref_max_ms=300 and enable canonicalize_prefix in cache lookup for the canary group. I'll also queue a rollback of the kernel selection to a hotfix branch if hit-rate doesn't recover in 15m. Action items: - nate: run replication lag trace and adjust heartbeat - chen: patch cache lookup canonicalization + tests - sara: run microbench for tokenization offsets and KV key diffs

sara: For the microbench: run `kv_cache.debug.probe --seq-dist "short,mid,long" --kernel attention-fused,baseline --normalize true` and export the `key_diff` report. That shows direct mismatches between generated keys.

nate: I'll spin the canary at 3% in eu-west and watch `cache_hit_rate`, `replication_cf_lag`, and `route_fallback_rate`. Will post results in 10m. :eyes: 

morgan: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. If canary recovers hit-rate we can ship a proper patch; otherwise rollback and deeper root-cause. :thumbsup:
